metadata.subject: Spot colours under PDF/X-4 (ISO 15930-7): /Separation inks, a /DeviceN mix, per-bar chart colours (pdfnative ≥ 1.9.0)
metadata.keywords: print, spot colour, separation, devicen, pdf/x-4, prepress

outputIntent.info: A structurally valid, colourimetrically meaningless CMYK press profile shipped with the samples. Ask your printer for their ICC profile (e.g. ISO Coated v2, GRACoL).

blocks.text: Brand blue on its own plate

Rendered with: pdfnative render --input 08-spot-colours.json --pdfx pdfx4 --output-intent-icc synthetic-cmyk.icc --font latin --lang latin --trapped false --strict. Every ink a colour names is declared in layout.print.spotColours with its CMYK alternate; a RIP that knows the ink puts it on its own plate, a composite proof paints the alternate.
This paragraph is PANTONE 300 C at 100 %: a /Separation colour space named after the ink, with [100, 44, 0, 0] as the alternate.
The same ink at a 40 % tint — one number in the content stream; the tint transform does the rest.
PANTONE 1235 C, the brand yellow, as a second separation.
Blue over a spot varnish: a /DeviceN space over both inks (five-element array, /Colorants attributes) whose type-4 tint transform adds the two alternates.

blocks.title: Each bar painted in its plate's ink (ChartSeries.colors)

blocks.text: An undeclared ink, or a mix of inks with different alternate spaces, is refused by the engine before any byte is written (E_INPUT); --dry-run reports the same refusal.
